transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-15 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Marcus Wu (Redwood CSM), Lena Ortega (SentinelPay Platform Lead), Samir Patel (Backend Engineer), Olivia Chen (Security)

Auto-generated summary: see summary field above.

[00:00] Jordan Kim: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, quick check — can you hear me ok?
[00:06] Lena Ortega: yes, loud and clear. thanks Jordan.
[00:09] Jordan Kim: cool. quick agenda: we triage the latency regression you saw in the sandbox post SDK 2.1.0, walk through function-calling fallbacks you captured, and then a quick security/ops checklist for the next pilot week. Priya, Marcus quick intro?
[00:22] Priya Shah: hi everyone, Priya here, I'm the SE working on the SDK hooks and runtime traces, I'll lead the repro instrumentation.
[00:29] Marcus Wu: Marcus from CSM, triage coordination and logistics.
[00:32] Samir Patel: Samir from backend, we ran the smoke tests yesterday and saw about a 30 to 40% increase in p95 on our main route.
[00:40] Jordan Kim: ok that's the number we expected from your note. can you describe the route and payload size?
[00:45] Samir Patel: yeah it's a transactional enrichment route — average 1.2k tokens per request, some have persistent KV cache hits, some cold cache. payloads include multiple tool calls, we call two internal functions via the SDK's function-calling API.
[00:59] Priya Shah: just to clarify — are you using Redwood Hosted or Dedicated for the sandbox runs?
[01:04] Samir Patel: sandbox is hitting Redwood Hosted initially, but we spun up a dedicated pool yesterday for the repro and saw similar tails.
[01:11] Olivia Chen: and from security we want to confirm no data leakage, so we're running the tests in a VPC peered environment.
[01:18] Jordan Kim: perfect. ok so timeline: SDK 2.1.0 added buffered batching changes and a slight change in the function-calling backoff path. that could affect tail if a blocking flush occurs. Priya has a hypothesis.
[01:30] Priya Shah: yeah, hypothesis — the buffered batching commit introduced a short window where the KV cache check and function-call orchestration are serialized, which at high concurrency can create head-of-line blocking. in simpler terms, a request waiting on a function call can stall subsequent token streams in the same batch.
[01:50] Samir Patel: that makes sense, we did see correlation between concurrency spikes and the p99.
[01:55] Lena Ortega: is this the same as continuous batching or is it the SDK buffer? I thought Redwood runtime did continuous batching.
[02:03] Priya Shah: good question — Redwood runtime still does continuous batching at the serving layer, but the SDK's local buffering is intended to better pack short sequences. the interaction between local SDK buffer and server-side continuous batching is where the timing mismatch happens.
[02:20] Jordan Kim: so two levers: we can disable local buffering in the SDK for critical routes (config flag), or adjust batch windows server-side. both have cost/latency tradeoffs.
[02:31] Samir Patel: can you force the SDK to treat function calls as non-blocking? we prefer returning partial structured output and letting the backend invoke tools async.
[02:40] Priya Shah: currently function-calling in the SDK has two modes — sync by default, and a beta async pattern. the beta async is available but needs a tiny runtime change to preserve ordering for some downstream apps. we can enable it for your pilot route as a feature flag.
[02:56] Olivia Chen: from security, async function-calls mean more event traffic — we need KMS lifecycle for payloads in transit and audit logs for each invocation. can Redwood provide a per-invoke audit log blob?
[03:10] Jordan Kim: yes, we can emit per-invoke audit events in the console and ship them to your S3 or SIEM. Marcus will link the audit docs after this call.
[03:18] Marcus Wu: noted, I'll share the compliance bundle.
[03:21] [00:04:00] Lena Ortega: ok on structured-output, we had two failures yesterday where the SDK returned slightly malformed JSON — extra trailing comma in a list — the validator crashed and the whole route failed.
[03:34] Priya Shah: ugh, trailing commas — that's probably from the new structured output serializer in the SDK that attempted to be permissive. we reverted strict mode for some types in 2.0 and 2.1 tried to be tolerant. we should flip it back to strict for schema'd routes.
[03:49] Samir Patel: do you have an automated schema validator we can run client-side?
[03:54] Priya Shah: yes, we have the sdk-schema-checker module in the debug build — it validates output against JSON schema and can emit a failure code rather than throwing. we'll include that in the instrumented build.
[04:07] Jordan Kim: action: Priya to add schema-checker to debug SDK and send minimal repro scripts.
[04:13] [00:08:00] Samir Patel: about the KV cache — we noticed K V cash hits were inconsistent, logs show both hits and misses in close succession for identical keys. not sure if that's a telemetry issue or real.
[04:25] Priya Shah: sometimes the metric aggregation at SDK level has a race where a cache miss and a parallel cache fill get recorded weirdly. we'll instrument stronger counters and add consistent correlation ids.
[04:36] Jordan Kim: for the latency sweep we want p50/p95/p99 and also continuous batching window histograms. Jordan (me) will run a 10k-token sweep on dedicated and hosted to compare.
[04:48] Lena Ortega: we also want to see quantization differences — some of our routes use a quantized model variant for cost. does Redwood adjust kernels for quantized models?
[04:58] Priya Shah: yes, runtime selects different kernels based on quantization type and sequence_len distribution — we'll include model variant in sweep.
[05:06] [00:12:00] Olivia Chen: security quick question — do you store any customer payloads at rest in Hosted by default?
[05:12] Jordan Kim: Hosted optionally caches logs for debugging but you can opt-out; for Dedicated there's no persistent customer data retention by default and Private keeps everything in your VPC. we'll share the exact retention settings.
[05:22] Olivia Chen: and KMS?
[05:24] Marcus Wu: we support customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated; Hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS but we can bring-key under enterprise contract.
[05:33] Lena Ortega: good. ok, timeline for next week?
[05:36] Jordan Kim: immediate: Priya posts instrumented SDK by Monday, Marcus shares security pack by Friday, Jordan to run benchmark and post raw traces. customer to provide failing payloads ASAP.
[05:48] Samir Patel: we'll extract failing examples and push to the repro repo, link in the shared sheet.
[05:53] Priya Shah: small note — there was a subtle naming mismatch in your function definitions, SDK expects a stable function_id, not a descriptive name; if your CI rewrites names on deploy that can break structured parsing.
[06:06] Samir Patel: oh, that's likely from our deploy templating. we'll freeze function ids for the pilot.
[06:11] [00:20:00] Jordan Kim: ok let's quickly demo the flag to disable local buffering in the SDK — Priya, can you run the toggle and show a micro benchmark?
[06:19] Priya Shah: sure — share screen — this is a small script hitting /generate with buffer=false. p95 drops by about 18% but p50 increases slightly because less packing. (screen noise, clicks)
[06:31] Lena Ortega: that's an acceptable trade for critical routes. we'll keep non-buffered for transaction routes and buffered for lower priority.
[06:38] Olivia Chen: flagged for compliance: ensure audit logs include both buffered and non-buffered invocation metadata.
[06:45] Marcus Wu: will add that to the audit deliverable list.
[06:49] [00:28:00] Jordan Kim: any blockers to Redwood enabling async function-calls for your route?
[06:55] Samir Patel: conceptually fine, but we need ordering guarantees for a subset of events — can we async some function calls and keep others sync?
[07:03] Priya Shah: yes, we can per-route annotate calls as sync/async in the SDK config. will include a sample in the instrumented build.
[07:10] Jordan Kim: last item — on-prem viability. Lena, you mentioned air-gapped concerns?
[07:14] Lena Ortega: yes, finance is pushing for Private in our region for data residency. we need an architecture discussion: footprint, patch cadence, key management, and SLAs.
[07:24] Jordan Kim: ok I'll book a 60-minute on-prem deep-dive with infra and security next week. action item for me.
[07:29] [00:36:00] Samir Patel: one final thing — we saw a double-invoke in logs where both the SDK and our orchestration invoked the same tool after a retry. could be due to backoff semantics.
[07:37] Priya Shah: yep that's retry-idempotency interplay — we'll add idempotency tokens to the next SDK build as an opt-in.
[07:44] Jordan Kim: great. recap of next steps and owners in the action items above. any final questions?
[07:50] Lena Ortega: none from me. thanks everyone.
[07:52] Olivia Chen: thanks — please send SOC2 artifact link and KMS notes.
[07:56] Marcus Wu: will do.
[07:58] Jordan Kim: thanks all, wrap up. next sync same time next week unless we need to meet earlier after repro. bye.
